HACKATHON GUARDRAILS (non-negotiable):
- DEADLINE: 2026-10-12T18:25Z. Feature freeze 2026-10-12T06:25Z. You work on ONE task; stop when its acceptance passes.
- Read docs/DESIGN.md sections named in your task before writing code. src/types.ts is the shared contract:
  if you need a change, make it minimal and say so in your final message.
- Touch only the files your task OWNS. Never edit another task's files, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, setups/, experiments/.
- Tests: `bun test <your test path>` must pass and `bun test` (whole suite) must not regress. Never modify existing tests
  unless your task says so. Fixtures are built by scripts from real samples, never hand-invented payloads.
- Commit in small steps as work lands, message prefix "<task id>: ". Never rewrite history. Never commit secrets or .env.
- Never describe unbuilt work as done in README/docs. No numbers in docs except those generated into docs/FACTS.md.
- Use `entire graph impact --symbol <name> --json` (or `entire graph query`) before editing an existing module, if available.
- Final message: what you built, test output summary, any types.ts change, anything you could not finish.
- Never start a command in the background or wait for a notification: this session ends when you stop. Run tests and builds in the foreground, then commit.

TASK T81 · W4 · neatlogs trace spool: a timed-out flush is retried, never lost
GOAL: Review traces keep getting dropped. Review 1b logged "Error flushing spans: Error: Request timed out … 0 spans exported, 3
dropped", so its neatlogs trace never arrived, and the rubric asks for before/after traces with the numbers compared. Make every run's
trace durable.
READ: src/obs/index.ts (initObs, withSpan, flushObs, trace id handling), src/obs/attributes.ts, the installed neatlogs SDK's type
definitions in node_modules/neatlogs/dist (the trace JSON it POSTs to /v1/trace; flushAllDetailed; endpoint/apiKey options),
scripts/obs-smoke.ts, src/cli.ts (command registry).
OWNS: src/obs/spool.ts (new), src/obs/index.ts (flush path only), src/cli/traces.ts (new), src/cli.ts (one registry line),
tests/obs-spool.test.ts
BUILD: Alongside the SDK, keep a local copy of each run's span tree as the trace JSON the SDK would send (same shape as /v1/trace). On
flush:
- if the SDK reports any dropped spans or throws, write .roster/traces/<trace-id>.json and print "neatlogs: trace <id> saved for retry"
- `roster traces flush` re-POSTs every saved trace to the neatlogs ingest endpoint (`x-api-key` from NEATLOGS_API_KEY, never printed)
  with 3 attempts and backoff, deletes each file on success, and prints the trace id and HTTP status per file
- `roster traces list` shows saved traces
Never log the API key, and never write it to the spool.
ACCEPTANCE: tests with a fake fetch: a failed flush writes the spool file; `traces flush` re-sends it with the x-api-key header and deletes
it on 200; a 500 keeps it; no key in any file. Whole suite unaffected.
TEST: bun test tests/obs-spool.test.ts && bun run typecheck
DO NOT TOUCH: anything outside OWNS.
